bull_bear.body:
- Disciplined growth: net debt/underlying EBITDA 3.3x, net debt/equity 1.2x maintained as guardrails.
- Self-funding via strong subsidiary cash generation; backward integration (wafer/ingot) to capture more value chain.
- Coal asset sale as potential deleveraging/value-crystallization optionality.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Transmission/ROW & TBCB/ISTS evacuation delays — primary cause of capex slippage; recurring risk.
- Solar curtailment / temporary-GNA risk on RE evacuation.
- Mundra: remaining 4 states' SPPA signing pending (regulatory approval risk); Section 11 interim.
- Indonesian coal export tax/royalty (under discussion) — mitigated by pass-through.
- Delhi regulatory true-ups are lumpy/unpredictable — FY27 reported numbers could be lower if fewer approvals; regulatory-asset wind-down dependence on regulator affidavit.
- Tata Projects return to profit not yet proven.
- Deferred-tax asset recognition flatters PAT (non-cash, one-off).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, measured, candid. CEO repeatedly stresses "calibrated growth" and balance-sheet discipline; acknowledged capex miss openly and attributed to deliberate caution on GNA. Strong transparency on subsidiary numbers; offered to improve disclosure quality. Tone constructive and credible, not promotional.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The capex "miss" is partly self-imposed discipline (refusing to strand assets on temporary GNA) — quality of growth, not weakness.
- DCR/domestic-cell mandate (1-Jun-2026 rooftop; 1-Sep-2025 utility tenders; 1-Jun-2028 wafers) structurally captures Tata Power's captive manufacturing — vertical integration becomes a regulatory moat.
- Future RE economics shift to hybrid+storage bundled deals with C&I/data centres — higher returns than the depressed pure-RE auction tariffs of FY24–25.
- Two PAT boosters this year (INR783 cr Delhi true-ups + INR250 cr deferred tax) are partly non-recurring — watch FY27 base.
- Nuclear SMR is a long-dated free option, not yet in numbers.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Deck frames the balance sheet as a "Comfortable Debt Position For Sustainable Growth"; Net Debt Rs 61,238 Cr in Q1 FY27 vs Rs 56,122 Cr in Q4 FY26 and Rs 47,578 Cr in Q1 FY26, with the increase attributed to higher capex and WC requirements.
- Net Debt to Equity 1.25 in Q1 FY27 (1.18 in FY26, 2.19 in FY19); Net Debt to Underlying EBITDA 3.41 in Q1 FY27 (3.34 in FY26, 5.19 in FY19), based on trailing twelve months.
- Credit ratings (Consolidated, current): CRISIL AA+/Stable, India Ratings AA+/Stable, ICRA AA+/Stable, CARE AA+/Stable, S&P Global BBB/Stable, Moody's Ba1/Positive — an upgrade path from AA/Stable and BB+/Stable in FY23.
- Total Gross Debt (LT + ST) of Rs 74,069 Cr at Q1 FY27, with RE Gencos the largest block at Rs 31,734 Cr and Tata Power Standalone at Rs 23,966 Cr; cash & cash equivalents Rs 12,831 Cr and networth Rs 49,026 Cr.
- Risk mitigation on the growth pipeline: land acquired/visibility for all under-construction RE projects, transmission connectivity secured, and 87% of pipeline RE projects tied in LT PPA.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- India's largest integrated power company, present across generation, transmission, distribution and trading, giving diversification across the value chain
- Diversified generation fuel mix (thermal, hydro, waste heat recovery, wind, solar) and geographic footprint across India and 7 other countries
- Industry-leading yield of more than 95% across cell and module lines at its 4.3 GW solar cell and module manufacturing facility
- Sustained deleveraging track record: consolidated Net Debt/Underlying EBITDA reduced from 6.1x to 3.3x over the past decade, with an 'industry leading' Debt/Equity of 1.2x
- Long-standing regulated distribution franchises via public-private partnerships in Delhi and Odisha, plus a long-term regional hydro partnership with Druk Green in Bhutan
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Mundra Thermal Plant operational and regulatory dependency — The 4,150 MW Mundra plant was suspended from July 3, 2025 for overhauling, cutting sales from 21,776 MUs in FY25 to 5,884 MUs in FY26. Continued operation currently rests on successive short-term Ministry of Power Section 11 directions (the latest extends operations only to June 30, 2026) and on completing a Supplementary PPA with procurers other than GUVNL, whose approvals remain in progress.
- Imported coal price and fuel-supply exposure — Mundra's economics depend on imported coal; the Company holds a 30% stake in PT Kaltim Prima Coal specifically to hedge imported coal price fluctuations, and has had to source lower-cost coal from diversified geographies and increase blending of lower-calorific-value coal to mitigate losses — evidence of structural exposure to coal price and supply-chain volatility.
- Unplanned outage / technical risk across the conventional generation fleet — Plant availability swings sharply year to year: Trombay recovered to 93.2% in FY26 from just 76.6% in FY25 after a fire-related Unit 5 shutdown, while Bhira Hydro's availability fell to 89.4% during a planned 115-day overhaul — showing fleet earnings are sensitive to unplanned technical outages and major maintenance events.
- Minority-partner / JV structure in key generation assets — Material generation assets are held through JV-type subsidiary structures with external partners — Maithon Power (Tata Power 74%, DVC 26%) and Industrial Energy Limited (Tata Power 74%, Tata Steel 26%) — so a meaningful share of consolidated generation earnings and capital decisions is subject to partner alignment.
- Earnings dependency on discrete regulatory/tax determinations — Reported subsidiary profitability has relied on one-off regulatory and tax items — Maithon Power's FY26 PAT was supported by a CERC regulatory order of Rs 23 crore and new TRAS ancillary-market participation, and Industrial Energy Limited's higher PAT relied on recognition of a Rs 84.72 crore MAT credit entitlement — indicating sensitivity of reported earnings to regulatory/tax outcomes outside the Company's direct control.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **Solar manufacturing**: stabilized, high yields, INR857 cr PAT (>2x). Captive cell/module to feed own IPP + rooftop; DCR mandate (effective 1-Jun-2026) a tailwind.
- **Odisha DISCOM**: standout, INR809 cr PAT; further loss-reduction runway.
- **Delhi (DDL)**: prior-period regulatory true-ups (INR783 cr FY26); regulatory asset to amortize over 6 yrs to 2032 (SC/APTEL monitored, affidavit given).
- **Mumbai (IEL/Mumbai Transmission)**: recurring ~INR1,000 cr/yr capex, RoE on 30% equity (70-30) — steady regulated growth.
- **Tata Projects**: legacy DFC/Barmer refinery projects nearly done; expected to return to profit FY27.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Tata Power is proposing to upstream its solar value chain into Solar PV ingot and wafer manufacturing, with planned capacity of up to 10 GW built in two phases of 5 GW each (aligned with ALMM List III), estimated investment of ~Rs 6,500 crore and a projected ~5-year payback. In Bhutan, the Company entered two new hydro JVs with Druk Green Power Corporation during the year — the 600 MW Khorlochhu Hydro Power Project (40% stake in KHPL) and the 1,125 MW Dorjilung Hydro Power Project (40% stake in DHPL) — and separately identified/added the 404 MW Nyera Amari I & II Integrated Hydropower Project to DGPC's portfolio. TPREL's renewable energy portfolio stood at 11.6 GW, including 5.1 GW under various stages of implementation; clean and green capacity under construction reached 9,630 MW (including 2,447 MW of Complex/FDRE projects) against a 70%-by-2030 clean-and-green portfolio target. TP Solar's Tirunelveli facility produced 3,825 MW of modules and 3,759 MW of cells at yields of 96% and 93% respectively, and is now on the BNEF Tier-1 Manufacturers List and ALMM List II. Rooftop solar crossed 3,70,000 installations nationally with cumulative capacity over 4.8 GWp (115% y-o-y revenue growth), and the EV charging network reached 2,00,000+ home chargers, 5,800+ public/semi-public points, 1,200+ e-bus points and 1,160+ fast-charging points across 254+ highway stretches. On transmission, the Company delivered 732 ckm of lines during the year (765 kV Mainpuri-Bara, Mainpuri-Unnao and 400 kV Gonda-Tanda/Tanda-Basti under the SEUPPTCL project; 77 ckm 400 kV Koteshwar-Rishikesh under NRSS), received an LOI from RECPDCL to acquire the 226 ckm Jejuri-Hinjewadi Power Transmission project, and separately reported commissioning of 929 ckm plus securing 226 ckm of transmission projects supporting evacuation in Maharashtra, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh plus NCR data-centre substation demand; total transmission capacity reached 7,403 ckm including 1,841 ckm under construction, against a >10,000 ckm-by-2030 target. The Mundra Thermal Power Plant was suspended from July 3, 2025 for overhaul; a Supplementary PPA was executed with GUVNL and the MoP issued fresh Section 11 directions permitting Mundra operations from April 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026 on SPPA terms while approvals from remaining procurers are pursued. On the thermal/hydro/nuclear cluster, the Company continues operating its 8.8+ GW thermal portfolio while developing 4.5+ GW of hydro and pumped storage opportunities, and is working with a few state governments on nuclear-plant feasibility assessment with geotechnical studies under progress. Odisha DISCOMs delivered a 2% AT&C loss reduction with 50+ lakh smart meters installed, TPDDL commissioned India's first Micro Substation with Power Voltage Transformer (with Nissin Electric) at RG22 Grid Delhi, and Tata Power Trading Company launched a Cooling-as-a-Service business with a pipeline of 2+ lakh tons of refrigeration and 25 new HVAC-optimisation projects worth Rs 5.6 crore.

outlook.body:
- FY27 outlook: continued demand growth momentum, rising renewable share in the capacity mix, improved supply-demand balance, policy push for efficiency improvement and decarbonisation, and increasing need for dispatchable round-the-clock green power
- Renewable energy segment: customer demand shifting towards integrated and complex energy solutions, acceleration in storage deployment, gradual easing of PPA bottlenecks, and strong distributed solar growth
- Transmission & distribution segment: continued AT&C loss reduction, faster smart meter deployment, grid expansion with policy support, and improved DISCOM viability through private-sector participation
- New-age energy solutions: potential growth in rooftop solar adoption via the PM Surya Ghar Yojana, evolution of Energy-as-a-Service and complex round-the-clock RE solutioning for C&I consumers, scaling of distributed energy solutions, storage adoption acceleration, and evolution of clean energy markets (VPPAs, carbon markets)
- Thermal, hydro and nuclear: stable role of thermal for base load with increased focus on flexibilisation, hydro and pumped storage capacity expansion, and gradual nuclear scale-up supported by the SHANTI Bill and Nuclear Energy Mission for Viksit Bharat
- Company response to sector trends: scaling clean energy capacity (47% of the generation portfolio already clean and green) and leveraging digitalisation to enhance efficiency, reliability and complex green power solutioning
- Solar EPC segment ended the year with a third-party EPC order book of ₹766 crore
- Rooftop solar segment ended the year with an order book of ₹898 crore
- Tata Power Trading Company Limited's newly launched Cooling-as-a-Service (CaaS) business has a pipeline of 2+ lakh tons of refrigeration and 25 new HVAC-optimisation projects acquired worth ₹5.6 crore

risks.note: The 4,150 MW Mundra plant was suspended from July 3, 2025 for overhauling, cutting sales from 21,776 MUs in FY25 to 5,884 MUs in FY26. Continued operation currently rests on successive short-term Ministry of Power Section 11 directions (the latest extends operations only to June 30, 2026) and on completing a Supplementary PPA with procurers other than GUVNL, whose approvals remain in progress.
risks.risk: Mundra Thermal Plant operational and regulatory dependency

risks.note: Mundra's economics depend on imported coal; the Company holds a 30% stake in PT Kaltim Prima Coal specifically to hedge imported coal price fluctuations, and has had to source lower-cost coal from diversified geographies and increase blending of lower-calorific-value coal to mitigate losses — evidence of structural exposure to coal price and supply-chain volatility.
risks.risk: Imported coal price and fuel-supply exposure

risks.note: Plant availability swings sharply year to year: Trombay recovered to 93.2% in FY26 from just 76.6% in FY25 after a fire-related Unit 5 shutdown, while Bhira Hydro's availability fell to 89.4% during a planned 115-day overhaul — showing fleet earnings are sensitive to unplanned technical outages and major maintenance events.
risks.risk: Unplanned outage / technical risk across the conventional generation fleet

risks.note: Material generation assets are held through JV-type subsidiary structures with external partners — Maithon Power (Tata Power 74%, DVC 26%) and Industrial Energy Limited (Tata Power 74%, Tata Steel 26%) — so a meaningful share of consolidated generation earnings and capital decisions is subject to partner alignment.
risks.risk: Minority-partner / JV structure in key generation assets

risks.note: Reported subsidiary profitability has relied on one-off regulatory and tax items — Maithon Power's FY26 PAT was supported by a CERC regulatory order of Rs 23 crore and new TRAS ancillary-market participation, and Industrial Energy Limited's higher PAT relied on recognition of a Rs 84.72 crore MAT credit entitlement — indicating sensitivity of reported earnings to regulatory/tax outcomes outside the Company's direct control.
risks.risk: Earnings dependency on discrete regulatory/tax determinations
